label: Ruckus ZoneDirector 1200 WLAN controller
description: Ruckus ZoneDirector 1200 - enterprise-class smart WLAN controller on a thin desktop footprint: manages up to 150 Ruckus APs and 256 WLANs from one box, with 2x auto-sensing 10/100/1000 Mbps Ethernet ports (one of them a redundant standby) and an RJ-45 console port, powered by a 12V/2A external adapter, 25 x 15.93 x 3.16 cm, 1 kg.
notes: The port census is two lines of the datasheet, not a product-page guess: '**PORTS: 2 Ethernet ports, auto MDX, auto-sensing 10/100/1000 Mbps, 1 Console RJ-45 port**', and the hardware-features summary calls them '**Two 1000 Mbps ports for full redundancy**' - which is what makes a controller with a pair of ports one device rather than a switch: the second port is a standby, not a second uplink into a fabric. **Both ports are gigabit and there is no PoE on either** - the box is powered by a 12V/2A external adapter ('Output: 12V DC, 2A'), so `poeIn: 0` is stated rather than left to inference. **The console is an RJ-45 socket but is not an Ethernet interface**, so it carries no `connector` field: 802.1X and the management plane are reachable over `eth1`, and plugging a laptop into the console port asks for a serial session, which is exactly what the engine models. Not modelled: 'Support for 256 WLANs' and 'up to 150 RUCKUS APs' are capacities of the software, and the WLAN/AP-controller layer is not a port. Compare the FS controllers (#766-#769), which are the same shape of device with POE banks instead of a standby pair.
